subject: calderMobile
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: hanging mobile.
Style: Alexander Calder.
reasoning:
I'm thinking through a Calder-style hanging mobile design—static, no creature, joints optional but keeping it visually rich. I want the lowest hanging element to sit right near y=0 so the whole structure reads as suspended from above without touching the ground.

I'm planning a wire-and-shape hierarchy with colored flat extruded forms (red, black, yellow, blue, white) balanced on rod arms, built with helper functions that compute pivot points and endpoint positions for each branching arm, adding small beads and loops at the joints for visual detail.

Defining shape outline generators for leaf, crescent, and oval forms, then thinking through tree layout so the lowest point sits at y≈0 — I'm considering whether to shift the whole root object afterward or track the minimum y during a two-pass build.

Working out the exact mobile layout...

Continuing the right-side arm chain down to another sub-arm with a white disc, red kidney shape, and black spiky shape. Now I'm setting up a generic recursive data structure for shapes, arms, and hangs, defining a recursive placement function that positions each node by following the wire length down from its parent attachment point.

I'm defining the shape outline functions for discs, leaves, crescents, kidneys, and triangles, each parameterized by horizontal and vertical extents, plus small torus rings at hang points for the wire loops. Writing crescent outline math...

Defining more shapes...

Now I'm setting up a flat color palette (red, black, yellow, blue, white) plus wire color, and considering adding a small raised dot layer on some shapes using an extruded disc offset along the surface normal.

I'm computing the front-facing normal from the shape's orientation vectors, confirming thickness values for shapes and dots, and planning a dry-run pass that tracks minimum Y position so I can measure where shapes hang before actually emitting them.

Now I'm working out the arm end direction vectors using the tilt angle, setting up a builder helper for rods and torus-shaped loops, and adding a small ring at the top to represent the hanging hook. I'm offsetting everything upward so the whole mobile hangs correctly from that point.
